dazibao, a wall-mounted newspaper etc., as a popular form of communication in China.

Borrowed from Chinese 人參／人参 (rénshēn).

By analogy with ка̀ппути́ст (kàpputíst, “capitalist roader”), a calque of Chinese 走資派 /走资派 (zǒuzīpài, literally “one who takes the capitalist road”). By surface analysis, кап[италисти́ческий] (kap[italistíčeskij], “capitalist”) + путь (putʹ, “road”) + -изм (-izm, “-ism”).
From кап[италисти́ческий] (kap[italistíčeskij], “capitalist”) + путь (putʹ, “road”) + -ист (-ist, “-ist”), as a calque of Chinese 走資派 /走资派 (zǒuzīpài, literally “one who takes the capitalist road”).

parole.significato: capitalist roadist (relating to capitalist roaders or their alleged political beliefs, capitalist roadism)
parole.testo: From ка̀ппути́ст (kàpputíst, “capitalist roader”) + -ский (-skij, adjectival suffix), from кап[италисти́ческий] (kap[italistíčeskij], “capitalist”) + путь (putʹ, “road”) + -ист (-ist, “-ist”), a calque of Chinese 走資派 /走资派 (zǒuzīpài, literally “one who takes the capitalist road”).
Ultimately from Chinese 拉麵 /拉面 (lāmiàn), via Kazakh лағман (lağman), etc. Doublet of ра́мэн (rámɛn).

parole.parola: лучше один раз увидеть, чем сто раз услышать

parole.testo: Since the 1950s; Calque from Chinese 百聞不如一見／百闻不如一见 (bǎi wén bùrú yī jiàn, “it's better to see once than hear a hundred times”).

parole.significato: bok choy (Chinese cabbage), Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis

parole.significato: a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
parole.testo: From the quote by Chinese philosopher Laozi (c 604 bc - c 531 bc) in the Tao Te Ching, chapter 100: 千里之行，始於足下 (qiānlǐ zhī xíng, shǐyú zú xià, “a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step”).
From Chinese 韃子 /鞑子 (dázi), originally meaning any foreign ethnic group in Northern China, from Chinese 韃靼 /鞑靼 (Dádá), from Old Turkic 𐱃𐱃𐰺 (t¹t¹r¹).
